content: SECURITY DEFINER functions run as the creating role; if created by a superuser/postgres role they bypass RLS entirely (bypassrls). Used deliberately to avoid RLS-recursion when a function queries an RLS-protected table, but any such function is a de facto RLS bypass and must be audited. Functions are exposed via PostgREST/rpc() unless moved out of exposed schemas; grant EXECUTE only to necessary roles. Join tables still enforce their own RLS unless a security-definer function intentionally routes around it.
